researchQuestion: How does adding a second checkout server change customer waiting time and throughput under the same arrival stream?
scope: Finite, reproducible discrete-event queue simulation comparing one and two identical checkout servers with a bounded waiting room and customer balking.
mechanisms: FCFS assignment to the first available server
balking when all servers are busy and the waiting room is full
assumptions: Arrivals are generated from the top-level seeded Run stream
Each served customer has deterministic service duration equal to 1/service_rate
An arriving customer uses a free server immediately
Waiting customers are served FIFO and a free server is never left idle
The run starts empty and ends after all admitted customers complete service
No abandonment, priorities, setup time, or blocking
limitations: This is a theoretical queueing model, not a calibration to observed checkout data
Exponential interarrival times and deterministic service may not represent a particular store
Finite-horizon results can be sensitive to the seed and initial empty system
Waiting-room capacity changes admission as well as congestion, so server comparisons should report balking
Matched seeds make random generation reproducible but do not imply identical realized trajectories across configurations

mean_wait.description: Mean arrival-to-service-start time among served customers.

throughput.description: Served customers divided by the completion horizon.

utilization.description: Aggregate busy server time divided by servers times the completion horizon.

served_customers.description: Number of customers admitted and completed service.

balked_customers.description: Number of arrivals rejected because all servers were busy and the waiting room was full.

balk_rate.description: Balked customers divided by all arriving customers.
